title: Films, music, sport & free time
goal: Talk about what you're watching and listening to, review a film, recommend (or warn against) something, follow a cricket or football match, and talk about your hobbies.
intro:
Half of all conversation between friends in India is about films, songs, web series and cricket. This unit gives you the words people really use — most of them English, said with Hindi grammar (*hit, flop, boring, review, match, score*) — and the reactions that make you sound like a fan: **ज़बरदस्त!**, **पैसा वसूल!**, **टाइम वेस्ट है!**

The grammar is all about comparing: **better than**, **far better than**, **not as good as**, **the best ever**, **one of the best**, and **the more you…, the more…** (जितना … उतना …).

grammar.title: Comparisons in depth
grammar.body:
You know the basic pattern from unit 8: **X Y से ज़्यादा अच्छा है** 'X is better than Y' (literally 'X from Y more good is'). Here are the variations that make comparisons sound natural:

**Far / a bit more**: **से कहीं ज़्यादा** 'far more' · **से थोड़ा** 'a bit more' · **से बहुत** 'much more'
किताब फ़िल्म **से कहीं ज़्यादा** अच्छी है 'the book is far better than the film'

**Even more**: **से भी** — यह पिछले वाले **से भी** अच्छा है 'this is even better than the last one'. Without a 'than': **और भी** अच्छा 'even better'.

**Ready-made comparatives**: **बेहतर** 'better', **बदतर** 'worse' — no ज़्यादा needed: पहला पार्ट **बेहतर** था.

**Not as … as**: X **उतना** adj **नहीं** (है) **जितना** Y — यह **उतना** अच्छा **नहीं** था **जितना** पिछला 'it wasn't as good as the last one'.

**As … as**: Y **जितना** / Y **जैसा** — वह अपने भाई **जितना** लंबा है 'he's as tall as his brother'. **जितना** compares amount/degree; **जैसा** compares kind: **एक जैसा** 'the same, alike'.

**Equal**: **बराबर** — दोनों टीमें **बराबर** की हैं 'the two teams are evenly matched'.

Remember that adjectives like अच्छा and जितना/उतना agree with the noun: एक्टिंग हीरोइन **जितनी** अच्छी नहीं थी. Words like बेहतर, बोरिंग, ज़बरदस्त never change.

grammar.title: Superlatives: the best, one of the best, the best ever
grammar.body:
**सबसे** + adjective = 'the most…' (literally 'than all'):
सबसे अच्छा 'the best' · सबसे बोरिंग 'the most boring' · **सबसे ज़्यादा** 'the most' (amount)

**Within a group**: **… में सबसे** — इन सब **में सबसे** अच्छा 'the best of all these' · टीम **का सबसे** अच्छा खिलाड़ी 'the team's best player'.

**One of the best**: **सबसे** adj + **plural oblique noun + में से एक**:
यह उसकी **सबसे अच्छी फ़िल्मों में से एक** है 'this is one of her best films'.

**The best ever**: **अब तक का / की सबसे** … — **अब तक की सबसे** बोरिंग फ़िल्म 'the most boring film ever'. **का/की** agrees with the noun.

**This year's / in the world**: **इस साल की सबसे** बड़ी हिट · **दुनिया का सबसे** अच्छा खिलाड़ी.

In casual speech people often intensify instead: **एकदम** बेकार 'totally useless', **बहुत ही** अच्छा 'really, really good', **सबसे** बेस्ट (yes, people say it!).

The trap: after **में से एक** the noun must be **plural oblique**: फ़िल्मों, गानों, खिलाड़ियों — not फ़िल्म or फ़िल्में.

examples.en: This is the best film of the year.

grammar.title: The more…, the more…: जितना … उतना …
grammar.body:
Hindi builds 'the more…, the more…' with a matching pair: **जितना** 'as much as' in the first half, **उतना** 'that much' in the second:

**जितना** सुनो, **उतना** अच्छा लगता है 'the more you listen, the better it sounds'
**जितना ज़्यादा** खेलोगे, **उतना** अच्छा खेलोगे 'the more you play, the better you'll play'

Both words **agree** with the noun they describe: **जितनी** प्रैक्टिस, **उतना** मज़ा · **जितने** लोग, **उतनी** बातें. Used as adverbs they stay masculine: जितना सुनो.

The second half often adds **ही** for emphasis: जितना सोचो, **उतना ही** मुश्किल लगता है.

The same pair gives you 'as … as' (**उतना … जितना**, see comparisons) and two everyday fixed phrases:
**जितना हो सके** 'as much as possible' · **जितनी जल्दी हो सके** 'as soon as possible'.

The trap: English uses 'the' twice; Hindi never uses the word for 'the' here — just जितना … उतना.

examples.en: The more you listen, the better it sounds.

dialogue.title: After the movie
dialogue.setting: Pooja and Sameer, old friends, walk out of a cinema in Mumbai on a Friday night. Pooja talks to Sameer with the very close तू.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.en: So? How did you like the film?

lines.speaker: Sameer

lines.roman: sach bolūṃ? pahlā hāf zabardast thā, dūsrā thoṛā boriṅg.
lines.en: Honestly? The first half was brilliant, the second a bit boring.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: अरे नहीं! मेरे लिए तो यह इस साल की सबसे अच्छी फ़िल्म है।
lines.roman: are nahīṃ! mere liye to yah is sāl kī sabse achchhī film hai.
lines.en: Oh come on! For me it's the best film of the year.

lines.speaker: Sameer
lines.native: हीरो की एक्टिंग अच्छी थी, मानता हूँ। पर उसकी पिछली फ़िल्म इससे कहीं बेहतर थी।
lines.roman: hīro kī ekṭiṅg achchhī thī, māntā hūṃ. par uskī pichhlī film isse kahīṃ behtar thī.
lines.en: The lead was good, I admit. But his last film was far better than this.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: वो वाली? वो तो फ़्लॉप हुई थी!
lines.roman: vo vālī? vo to flop huī thī!

lines.speaker: Sameer
lines.native: फ़्लॉप होने से क्या होता है? जितनी बार देखो, उतनी अच्छी लगती है।
lines.roman: flop hone se kyā hotā hai? jitnī bār dekho, utnī achchhī lagtī hai.
lines.en: So what if it flopped? The more you watch it, the better it gets.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: ठीक है, ठीक है। वैसे गाने कैसे लगे?
lines.roman: ṭhīk hai, ṭhīk hai. vaise gāne kaise lage?
lines.en: OK, OK. Anyway, how were the songs?

lines.speaker: Sameer
lines.native: गाने तो पैसा वसूल थे। वो आख़िरी वाला गाना दिमाग़ से निकल ही नहीं रहा।
lines.roman: gāne to paisā vasūl the. vo āxirī vālā gānā dimāġ se nikal hī nahīṃ rahā.
lines.en: The songs were totally worth it. I can't get that last one out of my head.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: हाँ! अच्छा सुन, रविवार को इंडिया-ऑस्ट्रेलिया का मैच है। देखने आएगा?
lines.roman: hāṃ! achchhā sun, ravivār ko Iṇḍiyā-Osṭreliyā kā maich hai. dekhne āyegā?
lines.en: Yes! Oh listen, there's the India–Australia match on Sunday. Coming over to watch?

lines.speaker: Sameer
lines.native: पक्का! पिछली बार तो आख़िरी ओवर में हार गए थे, इस बार देखते हैं।
lines.roman: pakkā! pichhlī bār to āxirī ovar meṃ hār gaye the, is bār dekhte haiṃ.
lines.en: Definitely! Last time we lost in the final over, let's see this time.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: इस बार कप्तान कुछ अलग करेगा, देखना।
lines.roman: is bār kaptān kuchh alag karegā, dekhnā.
lines.en: This time the captain will do something different, you'll see.

lines.speaker: Sameer
lines.native: जितनी उम्मीद रखोगी, उतना दिल टूटेगा! हा हा।
lines.roman: jitnī ummīd rakhogī, utnā dil ṭūṭegā! hā hā.

culture:
Bollywood (and increasingly Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam films dubbed in Hindi) and cricket are the two great shared conversations of India. People quote film dialogues, sing old songs at parties (**अंताक्षरी** is the classic song game) and argue about which era of music was better — the **पुराने गाने** of the 60s–90s usually win with parents. Film talk is full of English: *hit, flop, superhit, review, trailer, OTT*, and reactions like **पैसा वसूल** 'worth the money' or **टाइम वेस्ट**.

During an India match, offices slow down, strangers ask **स्कोर क्या हुआ?** in the street, and everyone becomes a selector with strong opinions about the captain. Cricket talk mixes Hindi and English freely: *over, wicket, run, six, four*, with Hindi verbs: **विकेट गिरा**, **रन बनाए**, **मैच हार गए**. Football is huge in Kerala, Goa, Bengal and the Northeast and growing among young people everywhere. When asked about hobbies, people often answer with **मुझे … का शौक़ है**; saying you have none is a little odd, so have an answer ready!

tip.title: से कहीं ज़्यादा · उतना … नहीं जितना
tip.body:
- **X Y से ज़्यादा अच्छा है** — X is better than Y; **से कहीं ज़्यादा** = far more; **से भी** = even more than.
- 'Not as … as' = **उतना … नहीं जितना**: उतना अच्छा नहीं था जितना पिछला.
- 'As … as' = **जितना** (amount) / **जैसा** (kind). Both agree with the noun.

tip.title: सबसे — the best, one of the best
tip.body:
- **सबसे** + adjective = the most: **सबसे** बोरिंग फ़िल्म.
- 'The best ever' = **अब तक की सबसे** अच्छी फ़िल्म (का/की agrees).
- 'One of the best' = **सबसे अच्छी फ़िल्मों में से एक** — the noun goes plural oblique.

lessons.title: Songs and singers

tip.title: जितना … उतना … — the more…, the more…
tip.body:
- **जितना** सुनो, **उतना** अच्छा लगता है — the more you listen, the better it sounds.
- Both agree with their noun: **जितनी** जल्दी, **जितने** लोग, **उतनी** बातें.
- Fixed phrases: **जितना हो सके** 'as much as possible', **जितनी जल्दी हो सके** 'as soon as possible'.

lessons.title: Hobbies

tip.title: मुझे … का शौक़ है
tip.body:
- 'I'm into…, I love…' = **मुझे … का शौक़ है**: मुझे गिटार बजाने **का** शौक़ है (verb in the oblique: बजाने).
- Instruments are **बजाना**, sports are **खेलना**.
- The more you practise…: **जितनी** प्रैक्टिस करोगे, **उतना** अच्छा बजाओगे.
